Source: /docs/reference/evals.md

# Evals

Evals run fixed cases against an agent and record whether its turns,
tools, events, and output meet a contract. The
[Evals guide](/docs/evals.md) covers the regression workflow.

## Eval discovery and case IDs

Eval files live under the project-root `evals/` directory and end in
`.eval.ts` or `.eval.js`. The path under that directory becomes the
eval ID, so `evals/readiness.eval.ts` becomes `readiness`,
`evals/builds/api.eval.ts` becomes `builds/api`, and
`evals/builds/index.eval.ts` becomes `builds`.

Export one `defineEval` that sets exactly one of `test` or `cases`. A
case ID adds one path segment to the file ID:

```ts
export default defineEval({
  tags: ["smoke"],
  cases: [
    {
      id: "checkout",
      async test(t) {
        await t.send("Review checkout PR 42.");
        t.succeeded();
      },
    },
    {
      id: "search",
      async test(t) {
        await t.send("Review search PR 7.");
        t.succeeded();
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

Those cases are `prs/checkout` and `prs/search` when the file is
`evals/prs.eval.ts`. Case IDs must be unique single path segments.

A file can also export an array of `defineEval` calls, named with
zero-padded indexes such as `sql/0000`.

`iterations` repeats one datapoint 1 to 100 times. With
`iterations: 3`, `weather/nyc` runs as `weather/nyc/1` through
`weather/nyc/3`, and selecting `weather/nyc` runs all three.

## Eval configuration

Every suite needs `evals/evals.config.ts` with `maxConcurrency`:

```ts
import { defineEvalConfig } from "@grok/agent-sdk/evals";

export default defineEvalConfig({
  maxConcurrency: 20,
  judge: { model: "gpt-5.4-mini" },
});
```

| Option | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `maxConcurrency` | Required. Concurrent authored datapoints, from 1 to 200 |
| `timeoutMs` | Per-case timeout. A case or file value wins, then the CLI flag, then this config |
| `judge` | Default model for `t.judge` |
| `reporters` | Objects notified as cases and runs complete |
| `maxPlaygroundRuns` | Server-side batches kept in playground history. Defaults to 20 |

A case can override `description`, `tags`, `timeoutMs`, `iterations`,
`judge`, `reporters`, and `metadata`. Case metadata merges over file
metadata, and case reporters add to the file's reporters.

## Send turns in a case

`await t.send(message, options?)` runs one turn and waits until it
finishes or fails. Sends in one test share a session.

The returned turn has the assistant `message`, `sessionId`, `events`,
ordered `toolCalls`, `ok`, and a one-based `index`. Assertions on a turn
inspect only that turn, and assertions on `t` inspect the whole case.
The case also exposes `t.reply`, `t.events`, `t.turns`, `t.sessionId`,
`t.iteration`, `t.iterations`, and the timeout `t.signal`.

On the first send only, `workspaceFiles` seeds the session workspace
from a map of relative paths to content, and `workspaceDir` sets an
absolute working directory for a new local session.

`turn.expectOk()` throws when the turn failed, so later steps that
depend on it don't run.

## Trajectory assertions

Assertions record failures without stopping the test.

| Assertion | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| `t.succeeded()` | Run finished without failure |
| `t.calledTool(name, matcher?)`, `t.notCalledTool(name)` | A matching tool request occurred, or none did |
| `t.loadedSkill(name)` | Agent opened a named skill |
| `t.toolOrder(names)`, `t.eventOrder(matchers)` | Tool requests or event groups appeared in relative order |
| `t.usedNoTools()`, `t.maxToolCalls(max)` | No tool was requested, or the count stayed under the bound |
| `t.noFailedActions()` | No tool result failed |
| `t.calledSubagent(name, matcher?)` | Matching subagent call occurred |
| `t.taggedArtifact(kind?, predicate?)` | Matching durable artifact was tagged |
| `t.event(type, matcher?)`, `t.notEvent(type, matcher?)` | A matching session event occurred, or none did |
| `t.eventsSatisfy(label, predicate)` | Predicate accepted the event stream |
| `t.check(value, expectation)` | Value met an expectation builder |
| `t.score(name, value)` | Recorded a numeric score from 0 to 1 |

`t.requireToolCall`, `t.requireInputRequest`, and `t.require` return the
matched value and stop the rest of the test when nothing matches.

## Tool and event matchers

Tool matchers can narrow by `input`, `output`, `status`, and `count`.
Values can be literals, regular expressions, or predicates. Object
literals match partially:

```ts
t.calledTool("inspect_pr", {
  input: { verdict: "review" },
  count: 1,
});
```

Tool status is `completed`, `failed`, `pending`, or `rejected`.
Subagent matchers accept `output`, `status`, `count`, and `callId`.
Event matchers accept `data` and `count`.

## Expectation builders

`includes(string | RegExp)`, `equals(value)`, `matches(schema)`, and
`satisfies(predicate, label)` are hard gates by default, and
`similarity(expected)` is a soft score. `matches` accepts Standard
Schema implementations such as Zod.
`normalizedSimilarity(value, expected)` returns the same 0-to-1 value
that `similarity` uses.

## Severity and verdicts

Every assertion returns a severity handle:

```ts
t.calledTool("search").soft();
t.check(t.reply, similarity("Expected answer")).atLeast(0.8);
t.judge.closedQA("names the failing step").gate(1);
```

- `.gate(threshold?)` fails the case on a miss.
- `.soft(threshold?)` records a value and never fails the case.
- `.atLeast(threshold)` sets a soft bar, and a miss gives the case a
  `scored` verdict.

Case verdicts are `passed`, `failed`, `scored`, or `skipped`. A `scored`
case fails the run only under `--strict`.

## Judges

Judges grade what deterministic checks can't express:

```ts
t.judge.factuality(expected).atLeast(0.8);
t.judge.summarizes(expected).atLeast(0.8);
t.judge.closedQA("names the root cause").gate(1);
t.judge.sql(expected).atLeast(0.9);
```

Each judge grades `t.reply` unless you pass `{ on }` with another value.
Set judge options in the project config, the eval, the case, or the
call, and the nearest value wins.

`t.judge.model(prompt)` returns a raw model reply for custom grading.
Agent output is untrusted input, so wrap it with `fenceUntrusted` and
include `EVAL_JUDGE_INJECTION_GUARD` in the judge prompt.

## Judge host

A judge needs a judge model and a Cursor credential from
`agent-sdk login`, `CURSOR_API_KEY`, or `CURSOR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY`.
Without a usable credential the runner skips the case, and without a
judge model it fails the case and names where to set one.

## Datasets and fixtures

Load committed JSON, JSONL, or YAML relative to the project root:

```ts
import { defineEval, includes } from "@grok/agent-sdk/evals";
import { loadYaml } from "@grok/agent-sdk/evals/loaders";

const rows = await loadYaml<Array<{ prompt: string; expected: string }>>(
  "evals/data/cases.yaml",
);

export default rows.map(row =>
  defineEval({
    async test(t) {
      await t.send(row.prompt);
      t.check(t.reply, includes(row.expected));
    },
  })
);
```

## Reporters and results

Built-in reporters include `JUnit({ filePath, suiteName? })` and
`Artifacts({ dir })`. A custom reporter can implement `onRunStart`,
`onEvalComplete`, and `onRunComplete`.

JSON output has run totals and one result per case. Each result has the
case ID, verdict, assertions, session ID, inputs, final text, tool
calls, metrics, logs, duration, metadata, tags, and any error or skip
reason.

Each local run writes `summary.json`, `results.jsonl`, and
`evals/<case-id>.json` under `evals/<stamp>/` in the project state
directory. `--state-root` doesn't move them, and `--artifacts <dir>` or
`--no-artifacts` does.

## Select cases

```text
agent-sdk eval --dir . --list
agent-sdk eval --dir .
agent-sdk eval --dir . builds/checkout
agent-sdk eval --dir . --tag smoke
```

An ID matches itself and its descendants. Repeated IDs or tags combine
with OR, and a case must match both groups when you pass both.
[Run evals](/docs/reference/cli.md#eval) covers runs on a server.

## Suite summary cases

A case tagged `EVAL_SUMMARY_TAG` aggregates its file, so selecting it by
ID or with `--tag summary` also runs every other case in that file.

```ts
import { defineEval, EVAL_SUMMARY_TAG } from "@grok/agent-sdk/evals";

export default defineEval({
  cases: [
    {
      id: "checkout",
      async test(t) {
        await t.send("Review checkout PR 42.");
        t.succeeded();
      },
    },
    {
      id: "overall",
      tags: [EVAL_SUMMARY_TAG],
      async test(t) {
        await t.send("Summarize the checkout review.");
        t.succeeded();
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

---

Source: /docs/reference/extensions.md

# Extensions

An extension packages capabilities that would otherwise live under
`bot/`, such as tools, skills, and connections. One mount file adds them
under a namespace without copying their source into your project.

Extensions and Cursor plugins run as trusted host code. A namespace prevents name collisions but doesn't sandbox the package, so review the package before mounting it.

## Mount an extension

Install the package and add one file under `bot/extensions/`. The
filename becomes the namespace, so this mount contributes names such as
`ci__failed_jobs` and `ci__triage`. The `__` separator is reserved, so
root contributions can't impersonate a mounted one.

```ts
// bot/extensions/ci.ts
import ci from "@acme/ci-triage";

export default ci({
  org: "acme",
  token: () => process.env.BUILDKITE_TOKEN ?? "",
});
```

Pass `token` as a function so it reads `BUILDKITE_TOKEN` when a tool
calls it.

The extension validates its settings at load, so a missing or mistyped
setting fails `agent-sdk validate`.

Extension instructions follow the root agent's instructions.
The root agent still needs its own `bot/instructions.md`.

## Inspect a mount

Run discovery after mounting or upgrading an extension:

```text
agent-sdk validate --dir .
agent-sdk info --dir . --json
```

`info` lists each mount and every namespaced name it adds. The same
data appears under `extensions` in `GET /v1/info`.

`info` also shows the egress hosts and secret names each mount adds to
a hosted deployment, and `agent-sdk deploy` names every extension that
adds egress.

## Adjust a mounted extension

To replace or remove one contribution, mount as a directory. Put the
package mount in `extension.ts` and overlay the short name beneath it.

```text
bot/extensions/ci/
  extension.ts
  tools/
    job_log.ts
    retry_job.ts
```

```ts
// bot/extensions/ci/tools/job_log.ts
import { defineTool } from "@grok/agent-sdk/tools";
import {
  jobLogInput,
  readRedactedLog,
} from "../../../lib/ci.js";

export default defineTool({
  description: "Read a redacted CI log.",
  inputSchema: jobLogInput,
  execute: readRedactedLog,
});
```

```ts
// bot/extensions/ci/tools/retry_job.ts
import { disableTool } from "@grok/agent-sdk/extensions";

export default disableTool();
```

The first file replaces `ci__job_log`, and the second removes
`ci__retry_job`. Use the matching `disable*` helper for another slot, or
generic `disable()` when the file location already identifies it.
Validation fails when an overlay names a contribution the package
doesn't provide.

## Mount a Cursor plugin

`cursorPlugin()` mounts a vendored Cursor or Claude plugin the same way. Skills, commands, agents, and MCP servers become Agent
SDK skills, subagents, and connections.

```ts
// bot/extensions/notion.ts
import { cursorPlugin } from "@grok/agent-sdk/extensions";

export default cursorPlugin({
  path: "plugins/notion-workspace",
  variables: {
    NOTION_TOKEN: "${NOTION_TOKEN}",
  },
});
```

`path` is relative to the project root. `variables` fills the plugin's
MCP placeholders with `${NAME}` templates read when the connection
opens. An unresolved placeholder fails
validation instead of mounting a partial server.

Plugin rules and hooks aren't mounted. Overlay a generated
`mcp-connections/<server>.ts` file to replace or disable one plugin
server. OAuth-backed plugin servers use
[Host MCP OAuth](/docs/guides/mcp-oauth.md).

## Extension contents

| Ships under the namespace | Ignored |
| --- | --- |
| Instructions, tools, skills, MCP and host connections | `agent.ts`, storage, OpenTelemetry |
| Hooks, channels, schedules, and subagents | Playground code, custom sandbox backends |
| Artifact kinds and workspace seed files | Nested extensions |

`agent-sdk validate` reports unsupported paths.

## Build an extension

Lay out the package like the shareable part of `bot/`. The root
`extension.ts` supplies a description and validates the consumer's
settings.

```text
@acme/ci-triage/
  package.json
  extension.ts
  instructions.md
  tools/
    failed_jobs.ts
    job_log.ts
  skills/
    triage.md
  lib/
    buildkite.ts
```

```ts
// extension.ts
import { defineExtension } from "@grok/agent-sdk/extensions";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineExtension({
  root: import.meta.dirname,
  description: "Investigate failing Buildkite jobs.",
  config: z.object({
    org: z.string(),
    token: z.function().args().returns(z.string()),
    logTailLines: z.number().int().positive().default(200),
  }),
  hosting: () => ({
    egressDomains: ["api.buildkite.com"],
    secretNames: ["BUILDKITE_TOKEN"],
  }),
});
```

Package modules import this definition and read the validated
`extension.config`, with defaults applied. `hosting` adds its hosts and secret names to the mounting
agent's deployment. Publish the built entry point with its slot
directories and prose assets beside it.

Keep extension instructions and tool descriptions namespace-neutral
because the consumer chooses the prefix. [Project layout](/docs/reference/project-layout.md)
covers each slot's contract.

---

Source: /docs/reference/hooks.md

# Hooks

A hook subscribes to selected session events and can run a side effect after each matching event is recorded. Hooks run in the serving process for every session of the agent. They cannot change the turn, the prompt, or the reply. A handler that throws is logged and skipped.

Treat the event as read-only. Later subscribers see the same object. A hook is the wrong surface for anything that must run before the model or must fail a turn. See [Hook boundaries](#hook-boundaries).

`defineHook` is unrelated to [Cursor Agent hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks), the `.cursor/hooks.json` scripts that can observe, block, or modify the agent loop. Those still run inside a local session workspace.

## Author a hook

Author `bot/hooks/<name>.ts` with `defineHook` from `@grok/agent-sdk/hooks`. This hook meters tokens and pages on failure:

```ts
// bot/hooks/usage.ts
import { metrics } from "@opentelemetry/api";
import { defineHook } from "@grok/agent-sdk/hooks";

const meter = metrics.getMeter("acme");
const inputTokens = meter.createCounter("acme.tokens.input");
const turnFailed = meter.createCounter("acme.turn.failed");

export default defineHook({
  events: {
    async "turn.completed"(event, ctx) {
      if (ctx.session.purpose === "eval" || event.data.usage === undefined) {
        return;
      }
      inputTokens.add(event.data.usage.inputTokens);
    },
    async "turn.failed"(event, ctx) {
      const pagerUrl = process.env.PAGER_WEBHOOK_URL;
      if (
        pagerUrl === undefined ||
        ctx.session.purpose === "eval" ||
        event.data.status === "cancelled"
      ) {
        return;
      }
      turnFailed.add(1, { channel: ctx.channel.id });
      await fetch(pagerUrl, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          agent: ctx.agent.name,
          session: ctx.session.id,
          message: event.data.message,
        }),
        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000),
      });
    },
  },
});
```

Any module under `bot/hooks/` is a hook named by its path without the extension. `*.test.ts` and `*.spec.ts` are skipped. The default export must be `defineHook(...)`, names can't contain `__`, and an empty `events` map is skipped with a warning. `agent-sdk validate` reports all three. An extension mounts its hooks as `<ns>__<name>`, and `disableHook()` removes one. See [Adjust a mounted extension](/docs/reference/extensions.md#adjust-a-mounted-extension).

`agent-sdk init` scaffolds `bot/hooks/memory.ts`. Delete it to opt out of the journal. See [Memory](/docs/reference/memory.md).

Read hosted secrets inside the handler, not at module scope. See [Add egress and secrets](/docs/deployment.md#add-egress-and-secrets). Give outbound calls a timeout, because a stalled request blocks later handlers on that session.

## Events and payloads

Keys are event types from the [event vocabulary](/docs/reference/sessions.md#stream-events), or `"*"` for every event. A typed key narrows `event.data`, a `"*"` handler receives the union so you switch on `event.type`, and every event carries `{ type, index, sessionId, turnId?, at, data }`. Skip `*.appended` deltas when you want the final text.

| Event | `event.data` |
| --- | --- |
| `message.received` | `{ text }` |
| `turn.completed` | `{ result?, usage?, cost? }`. `usage` has `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, and optional `reasoningTokens`. `cost` has `totalUsd` and the `model` it was priced against |
| `turn.failed` | `{ message, status? }`. `status` is `"error"` or `"cancelled"` when present |
| `actions.requested` | `{ calls: [{ callId, toolName, args?, parentCallId? }], parentCallId? }`. One envelope per model step. `parentCallId` marks subagent work |
| `actions.completed` | `{ results: [{ callId, toolName, output?, isError, stubbed?, parentCallId? }], parentCallId? }`. Emitted when every call in that batch has a result |
| `action.result` | `{ callId, toolName, output?, isError, stubbed?, parentCallId? }`. Live per-call envelope. `stubbed` means a dry-run session answered a write without running it |
| `action.tool_retry` | `{ callId, toolName, attempt, reason, connection? }`. A read is running again after a transient failure. `attempt` is the try about to run |

The types are `SessionEvent`, `SessionEventType`, and `HookContext`, exported from `@grok/agent-sdk`.

## Handler context

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.session` | Read-only session info: `id`, `channelId`, `mode` (`chat` or `task`), `purpose` (`live` or `eval`), `auth`, plus `title` and `sdkAgentId` when set |
| `ctx.agent` | `{ name }` of the agent the event belongs to |
| `ctx.channel` | `{ id, continuationToken }`. The token is `null` when the session can't take follow-ups |
| `ctx.host.kv` | Durable JSON, shared by every session of the agent. Prefix keys with `ctx.session.id` for per-session state |
| `ctx.host.files` | Durable files, bound to this session. Pass `{ scope: "deployment" }` for agent-wide files |
| `ctx.host.mcp`, `ctx.host.github`, `ctx.host.slack` | The same shared clients tools get |
| `ctx.host.reminders` | Per-session [reminders](/docs/reference/schedules.md#reminders) |
| `ctx.artifacts` | Session-bound [artifacts](/docs/reference/artifacts.md) facade. `tag` fills in `sessionId` and `turnId` |
| `ctx.stateRoot` | Absolute path of the local state root. It resets when a hosted deployment is replaced. Keep derived state in `kv` or `files` |

## Hook dispatch

A hook runs after the event is recorded. It never delays the model.

| Rule | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Same session | Events dispatch one at a time |
| Eval sessions | The same stream fires. Skip metering or paging when `ctx.session.purpose === "eval"` |
| Host restart | Recorded events are not replayed into hooks, so a mirror needs no dedupe |
| Slow handler | Holds the next event's handlers on that session, not the model. Keep handlers short and queue anything slow |

## Hook boundaries

| You want to | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| Add context before the model runs | The channel's `send` message and `workspaceFiles`, `instructions.md`, skills, or `sandbox/workspace/` seed files |
| Reply on Slack, comment on a PR, or post any other delivery | The channel's `events` map, or the Slack and GitHub packs |
| Show PR progress (merge-box check, sticky banner) | `githubChannel({ progress: { commitStatus, banner } })`. See [GitHub agents](/docs/guides/github.md) |
| Gate a change on behavior | [Evals](/docs/evals.md) |
| Observe every session for audit, metrics, or a transcript mirror | A hook |

To act on a turn's decision, such as a label or a ticket, have the model record it with an authored [tool](/docs/reference/tools.md). A `turn.completed` hook then reads the recorded decision and acts on it through `ctx.host`.

## Test a hook

A hook definition is a plain object, so a unit test calls `hook.events["turn.completed"]` directly with an event and a stub `HookContext`. Discovery skips `*.test.ts`, so the test can live next to the hook.

| Command | What it reports |
| --- | --- |
| `agent-sdk validate --dir .` | Discovery errors and the empty-handlers warning |
| `agent-sdk info --dir . --json` | Loaded hooks under `agents[].hooks` |
| `agent-sdk run --dir . --message "…"` | Serve log on stderr, including `hook "<name>" handler for <event> threw: …` |

On hosting, read the same log with [`agent-sdk logs`](/docs/reference/cli.md#logs).

See also [Sessions](/docs/reference/sessions.md#stream-events), [OpenTelemetry](/docs/guides/opentelemetry.md), and [Channels](/docs/reference/channels.md#events).

---

Source: /docs/reference/http-api.md

# HTTP API

In the default multi-agent layout each agent serves its routes at
`/<slug>/v1/*`, and `--mode single` serves them at `/v1/*`.

Routes use the agent's HTTP auth chain, which defaults to
`localDevStrict()`. `--bearer-token` and `--allow-anonymous` replace it
with bearer or anonymous access. Built-in JSON
routes return errors as `{ ok: false, error: "<code>", message? }`, and
MCP uses JSON-RPC.

## Host routes

These routes need no auth.

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /` | HTML index of mounted agents |
| `GET /v1/agents` | JSON index of mounted agents, multi-agent layout only |
| `GET /<slug>/playground`, `GET /<slug>/playground/assets/:file` | The agent's playground page and assets |
| `GET /docs`, `GET /docs/*` | Documentation site |

`--no-playground` removes the index and playground routes, and
`--no-docs` removes the docs.

## Start a session

`POST /v1/session` opens a durable conversation.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/session \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"What can you do?"}'
# {"ok":true,"sessionId":"ses_…","continuationToken":"http:…",
#  "playgroundUrl":"…?sessionId=ses_…","traceUrl":"…/v1/session/ses_…/events"}
```

| Body field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `message` | Required user message |
| `title` | Display title |
| `dryRun` | Run read tools and stub write tools |
| `asOf` | ISO-8601 instant with a timezone. Sets `ctx.now()` and rejects omitted, relative, or later declared tool time arguments |
| `workspaceFiles` | Relative files added to the session workspace |
| `purpose` | `"eval"` marks regression traffic |

## Send a follow-up

`POST /v1/session/:sessionId` continues an existing conversation.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/session/ses_… \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"continuationToken":"http:…","message":"Make it shorter."}'
```

The route accepts any chat session, including one a custom channel created. Each accepted follow-up returns a new continuation token. A message to a busy session interrupts the active turn. A stale token or a task session returns `409`.

## Stream or replay session events

`GET /v1/session/:sessionId/stream` is the live NDJSON feed.

```bash
curl -N 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/session/ses_…/stream?startIndex=0'
```

It replays from `startIndex`, which defaults to `0`, then follows new
events. To reconnect without duplicates, pass the last index you
received plus one.

`GET /v1/session/:sessionId/events` returns a one-shot NDJSON dump, or
`{ sessionId, events, playgroundUrl }` with `?format=json`.
[Stream events](/docs/reference/sessions.md#stream-events) lists the event types.

## Manage sessions

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/session/:sessionId/stop` | Interrupt the active turn without sending another message |
| `GET /v1/sessions` | List sessions the caller owns |
| `GET /v1/session/:sessionId/cost` | Per-turn token usage and estimated cost |

Under `serve --dev` on loopback, the list includes every principal's
sessions.

## Call a tool without a model turn

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/tools/:toolName` | Run a server tool on `{ input, sessionId?, continuationToken? }` |

[Tools](/docs/reference/tools.md#call-a-tool-without-a-model-turn) covers session
binding, busy sessions, and error codes.

## Discovery routes

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/info` | Everything discovery found, such as the model, tools, channels, and diagnostics |
| `GET /v1/tools` | Server and advertised MCP tools as `{ name, title?, source? }`, optionally for one `session` or `continuationToken` |
| `GET /v1/tools/:name` | One tool's schemas, effect rules, execution mode, and source. An unknown name returns `404` with the available names |
| `GET /v1/logs?after=N` | Recent server logs and the next polling cursor |

`connectionErrors` names any connection that couldn't list its tools.

## List and download artifacts

`GET /v1/artifacts` returns the caller's `{ artifacts }`, newest-updated
first, filtered by `kind`, `sessionId`, and a positive `limit`.
`GET /v1/artifacts/:id/content` downloads an artifact's file or blob.
[Artifacts](/docs/reference/artifacts.md) covers tagging and record fields.

## Call custom channel routes

Authored routes mount under `/v1/channels/<id>` with their declared
methods and paths, behind each channel's auth chain.
[Route responses](/docs/reference/channels.md#route-responses) covers what a hosted
caller gets back.

## MCP endpoint

Both MCP routes use stateless streamable HTTP, so they take `POST` and
return `405` for `GET` and `DELETE`.

`/v1/mcp` serves `ask`, `check`, and `call_tool` when server tools
exist, behind the session API auth chain. `/v1/mcp/tools` serves only
deterministic server tools, behind the CLI-level loopback, bearer, or
anonymous auth chain. [MCP connections](/docs/reference/connections.md#peer-mcp-connection)
connects one agent to another.

## Playground eval routes

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/dev/evals` | List discovered cases and eval config |
| `GET /v1/dev/evals/runs` | List recent run snapshots, newest first |
| `POST /v1/dev/evals/runs` | Start `{ filterIds?, tags?, timeoutMs?, verbose? }`. Returns `202`, `404` for no match, or `409` while a run is active |
| `GET /v1/dev/evals/runs/:runId` | Progress and the final snapshot |
| `POST /v1/dev/evals/runs/:runId/cancel` | Cancel an active run. Returns `409` when it already ended |

Poll a run until it is `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. A case must match one entry from each of `filterIds` and
`tags` that you pass.

## Dev-mode routes

These routes exist only under `serve --dev`, where schedules and
reminders never fire on their own. `POST /v1/dev/schedules/:scheduleId`
dispatches a schedule once and returns `{scheduleId, sessionIds}`.
`GET /v1/dev/reminders` lists reminders, and
`POST /v1/dev/reminders/:reminderId` fires one.

## Status codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `202` | Accepted for asynchronous work |
| `400` | Invalid body, query, or tool input |
| `401` | No auth policy admitted the request |
| `403` | The caller doesn't own the resource |
| `404` | A named resource doesn't exist, or no eval case matches |
| `405` | The route doesn't accept this method |
| `409` | The resource's state rejects the request, such as a stale token or busy write |
| `500` | A write-effect tool can't create its session workspace (`workspace_unavailable`) |

## Related

- [Sessions](/docs/reference/sessions.md)
- [Channels](/docs/reference/channels.md)
- [Deployment](/docs/deployment.md)

---

Source: /docs/reference/instructions.md

# Instructions

Instructions are the always-on prompt for every turn. A root agent
requires them, and a subagent may inline `instructions` in `agent.ts`
instead.

## Authoring forms

| Form | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| `bot/instructions.md` | Most agents |
| `bot/instructions.ts` | Generated prompts. Default-export `defineInstructions({ markdown })` or a string |
| `bot/instructions/` | A long prompt split across files, joined in filename order |

```ts
// bot/instructions.ts
import { defineInstructions } from "@grok/agent-sdk";

export default defineInstructions({
  markdown: "You are the on-call assistant for the payments team.",
});
```

The `markdown` string is fixed when the file loads. See
[Add egress and secrets](/docs/deployment.md#add-egress-and-secrets) for
reading secrets inside a handler.

## Delivery

A local turn sends the instructions, with a short identity section, as the system prompt, and a turn in the cloud includes the same text in the first user message. Nothing is written to the workspace as `AGENTS.md`, but a parent directory's `AGENTS.md` can still reach a local session. See
[Local cwd](/docs/reference/agent-config.md#local-cwd).

## Contents

Keep instructions to a few lines that cover identity, when to use each
tool, and the output shape. A short version of the
[quickstart](/docs/quickstart.md) reviewer:

```md
# PR reviewer

You review GitHub pull requests. Be specific and brief.

1. Call `inspect_pr` first. Never judge a change you haven't fetched.
2. Match your review to the complexity it reports.
3. Never approve a draft.

End with one sentence: the verdict and why.
```

Name the tools and the decision rule, such as "use X before answering
about Y". State the output contract, including length and format, so
your [evals](/docs/evals.md) can gate it. Move occasional multi-step
workflows into [skills](/docs/reference/skills.md), which load on demand.

---

Source: /docs/reference/limits.md

# Limits

Cursor caps deployments for some teams. If your team has caps, these are the default values.

| Limit | Default | What counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner.deployments` | 20 | Each slug, running or stopped |
| `owner.deploysPerDay` | 100 per 24 hours | Each accepted deploy, including redeploys |

The error looks like this:

```json
{
  "error": "Your team has 20 of 20 deployments. Delete one with `agent-sdk deployment delete <slug>`, or contact support to raise the limit. Redeploying an existing slug doesn't count.",
  "code": "limit_exceeded",
  "limit": "owner.deployments",
  "max": 20,
  "current": 20,
  "docsUrl": "https://cursor.com/docs/bdk/reference/limits"
}
```

To free a slot, run `agent-sdk deployment delete <slug>`, or wait until the
oldest counted deploy is 24 hours old. A deploy can also answer `503` with a
`Retry-After` header, and you can retry it after that many seconds.

---

Source: /docs/reference/memory.md

# Memory

A memory hook appends one record per turn to a journal. The model reads
the journal with its file tools when its instructions send it there.

## Memory is on by default

`agent-sdk init` scaffolds `bot/hooks/memory.ts`:

```ts
import { memoryHook } from "@grok/agent-sdk/memory";

export default memoryHook();
```

It also adds a `## Memory` section to `bot/instructions.md`. The model
has no recall tool, so that section tells it when to read `memory/` and
to treat records as untrusted history. To add memory to an existing
project, copy both from a new `agent-sdk init` project. To turn memory
off, delete both.

## Journal records

After each turn, the hook appends one JSON line to
`memory/journal.jsonl`:

```json
{"at":"2026-10-01T16:42:09.118Z","sessionId":"5f0c2a9e-7d1b-4c43-9a6e-2b8f1e0d7c35","channelId":"slack","status":"completed","title":"Checkout flaky test","userMessage":"Why does acme/checkout fail on main?","result":"The cart test races the price service mock...","usage":{"inputTokens":18234,"outputTokens":912,"cacheReadTokens":15002,"cacheWriteTokens":0}}
```

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `at` | ISO-8601 time the turn finished |
| `sessionId` | Session that ran the turn |
| `channelId` | Channel that started the session |
| `status` | `"completed"` or `"failed"` |
| `title` | Session title, if set |
| `userMessage` | The turn's message, truncated |
| `result` | Final assistant text or failure message, truncated |
| `usage` | Token usage for completed turns |

As the journal grows, older records move to `journal-*.jsonl` files
beside it, so point the model at the whole `memory/` directory.

## Read memory

Local turns find the journal at `memory/` in the session workspace. On
Cursor hosting, Agent SDK tells the model where the journal is at the
start of each session. A session on a server you run yourself can't
reach the journal. Agent SDK rejects `workspaceFiles` and
`sandbox/workspace/` seed files under the reserved `memory/` path.

Local servers keep the journal in the project state directory. `agent-sdk run` and `agent-sdk eval` start with empty memory unless you pass `--state-root`, and hosted deployments keep the journal across redeploys.

## Caveats

- All sessions and users share one journal, so one person's messages
  can surface in another's session.
- Turning memory off keeps existing records. Locally, delete `memory/`
  in the project state directory to clear them. On Cursor hosting,
  [Privacy Mode](/docs/deployment.md#privacy-mode) applies.
- Anyone who can message the agent writes to the journal, so keep the
  scaffolded rule against following instructions found in records.
- Records can be dropped or arrive late. Keep state your code depends
  on in `ctx.host.kv` or `ctx.host.files`.

## Options

| `memoryHook` option | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `maxTextLength` | Truncation cap for `userMessage` and `result`. Default `2000` characters |
| `backend` | A `MemoryBackend` that replaces the default journal |

A `MemoryBackend` has `appendTurn(record, { stateRoot, agentName })`
and an optional `prepareSession({ stateRoot, agentName })` that runs
when a session starts. The model still looks in `memory/`, so tell it
how to read your records.

---

Source: /docs/reference/playground.md

# Playground

`agent-sdk serve` hosts a web playground at
`http://127.0.0.1:3000/playground`. When one server hosts multiple
agents, each agent's playground is at `/<slug>/playground` and `/`
lists them.

## Playground surfaces

| Surface | What you can do |
| --- | --- |
| Chat | Text and reasoning stream live, and tool calls appear inline with arguments, output, and errors |
| Slash commands | Run a custom channel route without path parameters from the composer. A `drive` route becomes `/drive <pr-url>`. GitHub and Slack ingress routes are excluded |
| Try | Call a custom channel route from the Agent tab and copy the request as curl |
| Runs | Search the sessions you own and eval runs, then open them in Chat, Trace, Raw, or Evals |
| Evals | List and run filesystem evals |
| Agent | Inspect discovered tools, skills, subagents, MCP connections, channels, and hooks |
| Raw | Inspect the selected session's event stream |
| Logs | Recent server log lines from `GET /v1/logs` |

In `--dev` on loopback, or with `--allow-anonymous`, the session list
includes every principal.

## Remote access

To open the playground through a tunnel or LAN address, start the
server with `--bearer-token <secret>` and paste the token into the
navbar's token field. See [Auth policies](/docs/reference/channels.md#auth-policies).

---

Source: /docs/reference/project-layout.md

# Project layout

An Agent SDK project keeps agent files under `bot/`, and each file's
path determines how Agent SDK loads it. [Evals](/docs/evals.md) live in
`evals/` at the project root, beside `bot/`.

```text
my-agent/
├── package.json
├── bot/
│   ├── agent.ts
│   ├── instructions.md
│   ├── tools/
│   │   └── approve_pr.ts
│   ├── skills/
│   │   └── pr-review.md
│   ├── mcp-connections/
│   │   └── linear.ts
│   ├── subagents/
│   │   └── reviewer/
│   │       ├── agent.ts
│   │       └── instructions.md
│   ├── extensions/
│   │   └── ci.ts
│   ├── channels/
│   │   └── github.ts
│   └── hooks/
│       └── audit.ts
└── evals/
    ├── evals.config.ts
    └── readiness.eval.ts
```

The root agent's name is the `name` in `package.json`, or else the directory name. When one server hosts multiple agents, each slug is the agent's directory name, and it must match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and can't be `v1`, `playground`, or `docs`.

## Folder reference

| Path under `bot/` | What it is | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.ts` | `defineAgent({ model?, local? })` | [Agent config](/docs/reference/agent-config.md) |
| `instructions.md` | Always-on system prompt, required on the root agent | [Instructions](/docs/reference/instructions.md) |
| `tools/<name>.ts` | One typed tool named after the file | [Tools](/docs/reference/tools.md) |
| `skills/*` | Procedures loaded on demand | [Skills](/docs/reference/skills.md) |
| `mcp-connections/<name>.ts` | MCP servers for the model, server tools, and handlers | [MCP connections](/docs/reference/connections.md) |
| `host-connections/<name>.ts` | MCP servers for host code and `mcp oauth`. The model never sees them | [MCP connections](/docs/reference/connections.md) |
| `subagents/<id>/` | Child agent directory with a required `description` | [Subagents](/docs/reference/subagents.md) |
| `extensions/<ns>.ts` or `extensions/<ns>/` | Extension or Cursor plugin mount. Its contributions become `<ns>__<name>` | [Extensions](/docs/reference/extensions.md) |
| `channels/<name>.ts` | HTTP routes under `/v1/channels/<name>` | [Channels](/docs/reference/channels.md) |
| `hooks/*.ts` | Observe-only event subscribers | [Hooks](/docs/reference/hooks.md) |
| `artifacts.ts` | Artifact kinds, the `tag_artifact` opt-in, and retention | [Artifacts](/docs/reference/artifacts.md) |
| `schedules/*` | Cron-driven runs | [Schedules](/docs/reference/schedules.md) |
| `reminders/*.ts` | Named reminder handlers | [Reminders](/docs/reference/schedules.md#reminders) |
| `sandbox/workspace/**` | Seed files copied into each local session workspace | [Sessions](/docs/reference/sessions.md#local-session-workspace) |
| `lib/` | Shared imports, never discovered | None |

Every eval project needs `evals/evals.config.ts`. Each
`evals/**/*.eval.ts` file is a suite whose case IDs come from its path.

A `.ts` file in a discovery folder loads as a definition, and an
unrecognized directory produces a validation warning. Agent SDK still
loads existing projects rooted at `agent/`.

## Inspect discovery

```text
agent-sdk validate --dir .    # diagnostics, non-zero exit on errors
agent-sdk info --dir .        # discovered surface
agent-sdk info --dir . --json # same shape as GET /v1/info
```

`serve` refuses to start on errors. Warnings do not block startup. When `info` omits a tool or channel, the file is in the wrong directory or has the wrong extension.

---

Source: /docs/reference/schedules.md

# Schedules and reminders

A schedule or a reminder lets an agent act without an inbound message.

## Schedules vs reminders

| | Schedule | Reminder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defined | At deploy time, in `bot/schedules/*` | At runtime, with `createReminder` or `host.reminders` |
| Scope | The whole agent | One conversation |
| Session | Starts a new task session, or hands off through `receive` | Wakes an existing conversation |
| Cadence | 5-field cron, in UTC, to the minute | `every`, `cron`, `delay`, or `at` |
| Dev mode | Manual dispatch only | Manual dispatch only, with timers off |

## Schedules

### Markdown schedules

A Markdown file with `cron:` frontmatter is a fire-and-forget task:

```md
---
cron: "0 9 * * 1-5"
---

Pull open incidents and post a summary to the metrics endpoint.
```

Each fire starts a task-mode session with the body as its prompt, and
the session runs to `session.completed` or `session.failed` without
follow-ups.

### Schedule handlers

A `run` handler can call tools or hand work to a channel, whose delivery
events then fire:

```ts
import { defineSchedule } from "@grok/agent-sdk/schedules";
import webhook from "../channels/webhook.js";

export default defineSchedule({
  cron: "*/30 * * * *",
  async run({ receive, waitUntil, appAuth, host }) {
    waitUntil(
      receive(webhook, {
        message: "Report any new critical alerts.",
        auth: appAuth,
      })
    );
  },
});
```

`defineSchedule` takes exactly one of `markdown` or `run`. `appAuth` is a
schedule-scoped principal for work the agent does on its own behalf. The
handler also receives `callTool`, for server-tool calls without a model
turn, and `host`, which holds `host.mcp`, `host.github`, `host.slack`,
and `host.reminders`.

### Dispatch a schedule

Schedules fire on their cron cadence on Cursor hosting and under
production `agent-sdk serve`. Run them in exactly one `serve` process
per project, or pass `--no-schedules` to turn them off. `serve --dev`
fires nothing on its own, so dispatch by hand:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/dev/schedules/heartbeat
```

The playground and `handle.dispatchSchedule("heartbeat")` dispatch the
same way.

### Schedules on Cursor hosting

Each deploy replaces the hosted schedules with the ones in
`bot/schedules/`, so a schedule you delete stops after your next deploy.

A `run` handler must finish in 26 minutes, including the work it passes
to `receive` and `waitUntil`. Module memory doesn't carry over to the
next fire, so keep state in `ctx.host.kv` or `ctx.host.files`. Each scheduled time
starts at most one run, and a stopped deployment skips its fires.

A schedule's name is its path under `bot/schedules/` without the
extension. On Cursor hosting, a name has 1 to 100 letters, digits, `.`,
`_`, `-`, or `/`, and starts with a letter or digit. A deploy can hold
at most 64 schedules, and `deploy` rejects one that breaks either rule.

## Reminders

A reminder belongs to one channel continuation, and it stays armed
across restarts. A recurring reminder works like `setInterval`, and a
one-shot reminder works like `setTimeout`.

Reminders take a prompt or a named handler. A prompt reminder sends
`prompt` into the conversation when it fires, and `until` tells the
model when to cancel it:

```ts
await handle.createReminder({
  purpose: "ci_recheck",
  channelId: "drive",
  continuationToken: "pr:acme/checkout#42",
  delay: "2h",
  prompt: "Re-check CI. Only act if still failing.",
  until: "Cancel once CI is green or the PR is merged.",
});
```

When host code must decide what happens on each tick, write a named
handler. It starts a model turn only if it calls `followup`:

```ts
// bot/reminders/ci_recheck.ts
import { defineReminder } from "@grok/agent-sdk/reminders";

export default defineReminder({
  async run({ args, followup }) {
    await followup({
      message: `Re-check CI for ${String(args.prUrl)}.`,
    });
    return { action: "delivered" };
  },
});
```

Pass its default export as `handler`, with serializable `args`:

```ts
import ciRecheck from "./bot/reminders/ci_recheck.js";

await handle.createReminder({
  purpose: "ci_recheck",
  channelId: "drive",
  continuationToken: "pr:acme/checkout#42",
  every: "30m",
  handler: ciRecheck,
  args: { prUrl: "https://github.com/acme/checkout/pull/42" },
});
```

Channel handlers, tools, and schedule runs get the same API as
`host.reminders`. `builtinTools: { reminders: true }` gives the model
`reminders_create`, `reminders_list`, and `reminders_cancel` for the
current conversation. See
[built-in tools](/docs/reference/agent-config.md#built-in-tools).

`--dev` doesn't fire reminders on its own. Dispatch one by hand, or call
`handle.dispatchReminder(id)` from code:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/dev/reminders             # list
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/dev/reminders/<id>  # fire one
```

Cancel a reminder when its subject ends, for example on
`pull_request.closed`. Keep wake prompts generic so the agent re-reads
live state.

---

Source: /docs/reference/sessions.md

# Sessions, events, and streaming

A session keeps one conversation, its workspace, and an append-only
record of every message and tool call.

## Session contents

Each session also has a channel, an authenticated caller, an NDJSON
event stream, and state that survives a restart. Sessions belong to the
principal that created them. Another caller gets `403` from that
session's routes.

## Session identifiers

| Identifier | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `continuationToken` | Continue a conversation through its channel |
| `sessionId` | Stream events, inspect state, or run a session-bound tool call |

Each channel picks its token format, such as a Slack thread or
`pr:owner/repo#1`. The built-in HTTP API returns an opaque token and
rotates it after each accepted follow-up, so a stale HTTP token returns
`409`.

## Session modes

HTTP sessions, channel `send`, Slack, and MCP `ask` create `chat`
sessions, which wait in `session.waiting` for follow-ups. Markdown
schedules and fire-and-forget dispatch create `task` sessions, which end
in `session.completed` or `session.failed`. A follow-up to a task
session returns `409`.

## Follow-ups

A follow-up starts a turn right away on an idle session. On a busy one, the channel decides what happens.

| Path | Busy-session policy |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP playground, `POST /v1/session/:id`, MCP `ask` | Preempt (the default). Interrupts the running turn, then runs the new message |
| Slack mentions, DMs, alert-watch | Coalesce. The running turn may pick up the follow-up at a tool boundary, and the rest become one turn when it finishes |

Pass `admission: "coalesce"` on `send()` to use the Slack policy from
other callers.

`POST /v1/session/:id/stop` interrupts a turn without sending a message.
The stream records `turn.failed` with `status: "cancelled"`, and the
session can take another follow-up. A Slack message that is only `stop`
or `@agent stop` does the same for its thread and clears pending
coalesced follow-ups.

### Track which follow-up reached the agent

Every `send()` returns a `deliveryId`. Pass your own, such as a webhook
delivery ID, or omit it to get a fresh `dlv_…` ID. A coalesced follow-up
reaches the agent in one of two ways.

| Path | Event | Field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steered into the running turn | `nudge.delivered` | `data.deliveryId` |
| Fell back to the next turn | That turn's `message.received` | `data.deliveryIds` |

`message.received` lists every send its prompt carries in arrival order,
so one turn can carry several IDs.

```ts
// In a route or channel hook: name the steer after the webhook delivery.
await send(`Incident ${incident.id} was acknowledged.`, {
  continuationToken: incident.id,
  admission: "coalesce",
  deliveryId: webhookId,
});

// In the channel's `events` map:
const steered = new Set<string>();
const prompted = new Set<string>();
const events: ChannelEventHandlers = {
  "nudge.delivered": async (event) => {
    if (event.data.deliveryId !== undefined) {
      steered.add(event.data.deliveryId);
    }
  },
  "message.received": async (event) => {
    for (const id of event.data.deliveryIds ?? []) {
      prompted.add(id);
    }
  },
};
```

In a local Slack session, a `nudge.delivered` event with no `deliveryId`
came from a new Slack message, not from a `send()` call.

## Stream events

Each NDJSON line is a `{ type, index, sessionId, turnId?, at, data }`
envelope. The `index` increases within one session, and `at` is an
ISO-8601 timestamp.

| Phase | Events | What they tell you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session | `session.started`, `session.waiting`, `session.completed`, `session.failed` | Creation, readiness, and task completion |
| Input | `message.received`, `nudge.delivered` | A prompt was accepted or reached a running turn. Both carry [delivery IDs](#track-which-follow-up-reached-the-agent) |
| Turn | `turn.queued`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed` | Queueing under [`maxRunningTurns`](/docs/reference/agent-config.md#concurrency), then status, result, and token usage |
| Steps | `step.started`, `step.completed` | Model step boundaries and duration |
| Reasoning | `reasoning.appended`, `reasoning.completed` | Streamed reasoning blocks |
| Reply | `message.appended`, `message.completed` | Text deltas and finished assistant messages |
| Tools | `actions.requested`, `actions.completed`, `action.result`, `action.tool_retry` | Tool names, arguments, outputs, and errors. `action.tool_retry` marks a read retried after a transient failure |
| Subagents | `subagent.called`, `subagent.completed` | Delegated work |
| Artifacts | `artifact.tagged` | An [artifact](/docs/reference/artifacts.md) was tagged |

`actions.requested` and `actions.completed` bracket each model step's
tool batch, and `action.result` carries each call live. Read
`turn.completed.data.usage` for token counts.
[HTTP API](/docs/reference/http-api.md#stream-or-replay-session-events) shows how to
follow the stream.

## Local session workspace

Agent SDK creates a workspace before the first local turn.

| Source path | Lands as |
| --- | --- |
| `skills/*` | `.cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| agent tools (`execution: "agent"`) | Scripts listed in the system prompt |
| `sandbox/workspace/**` | Seed files |
| per-send `workspaceFiles` | Files written before the turn |

On a local turn, Agent SDK sends the instructions as the system prompt, and on a turn in the cloud it includes them in the first user message. Nothing is written into the session workspace as `AGENTS.md`. See
[Instructions](/docs/reference/instructions.md).

A channel can give one session a different directory, such as a PR
worktree. [Agent config](/docs/reference/agent-config.md#local-cwd) covers what parent
directories add.

## Session storage

Local session state lives under `--state-root`, in a subdirectory named
for the slug on a slugged mount. Deleting a session directory removes
the session from the server.

## Inspect a saved event stream

`agent-sdk session get --file <state-root>/traces/<sessionId>.ndjson`
prints a saved trace's tool calls, reply, and token usage in the same
JSON shape as `run`. For a session on a running server,
`agent-sdk session get <sessionId> --view events` prints the raw event
list. The playground's **Trace** view shows a timeline.

## Related

- [HTTP API](/docs/reference/http-api.md)
- [Hooks](/docs/reference/hooks.md)
- [Tools](/docs/reference/tools.md)

---

Source: /docs/reference/skills.md

# Skills

A skill is an on-demand procedure in the `SKILL.md` convention. Agent SDK advertises each skill by its description, and the model loads a skill only when the task calls for it. Skills give an agent a multi-step workflow without carrying it in the always-on
[instructions](/docs/reference/instructions.md).

## Authoring forms

| Form | Reach for it when |
| --- | --- |
| `bot/skills/<name>.md` | Static Markdown. `description` frontmatter is optional and falls back to the first body line |
| `bot/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` plus siblings | A packaged directory with reference files. Requires `description` frontmatter |
| `bot/skills/<name>.ts` | Generated content, with `defineSkill` from `@grok/agent-sdk/skills` |

Use flat Markdown for static content:

```md
---
description: Use when a pull request needs a structured approval checklist.
---

# PR review checklist

1. Call `inspect_pr` and confirm required checks passed.
2. Summarize the PR title, author, and remaining risks.
3. Call `approve_pr` only after an explicit request.
```

Use TypeScript when the content must be generated or include inline
sibling files:

```ts
import { defineSkill } from "@grok/agent-sdk/skills";

export default defineSkill({
  description: "Research unfamiliar topics before answering.",
  markdown: "Gather evidence first, then answer with the key facts.",
  files: { "references/checklist.md": "# Checklist\n\n- Find sources.\n" },
});
```

## Skill delivery

Local sessions get each skill at `.cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in the session workspace, and the agent lists and loads them from there.

## Skills, instructions, and tools

Instructions stay in context on every turn. Skills hold procedures,
checklists, and house style that the model needs only sometimes. Put
anything that must be correct every time in a typed
[tool](/docs/reference/tools.md), where the model can't paraphrase it.

A description is a routing hint, so say when to use the skill, as the checklist example does. The model sees only the description before it decides to load the skill.

---

Source: /docs/reference/subagents.md

# Subagents

A subagent is a specialist child agent the model can delegate to mid-turn. Each one lives under `bot/subagents/<id>/` with a required `agent.ts`.

Add `instructions.md`, or inline `instructions` in `agent.ts`, for a custom prompt. Omit `model` to inherit the parent's model.

The parent model reads `description` to decide whether to delegate, so write it the way you write a [skill description](/docs/reference/skills.md#skills-instructions-and-tools).

The parent delegates through the `task` tool. A parent that limits its [built-in tools](/docs/reference/agent-config.md#harness-tools) must list `"task"`.

The stream records `subagent.called` and `subagent.completed`. `subagent.completed` has `isError: true` when the subagent failed or was cancelled.

```text
bot/subagents/researcher/
├── agent.ts            # description (required), model (optional)
└── instructions.md     # optional custom system prompt
```

```ts
// bot/subagents/researcher/agent.ts
import { defineAgent } from "@grok/agent-sdk";

export default defineAgent({
  description:
    "Background research: climate history, records, comparisons across many cities.",
  // model: omit to inherit the parent's model
});
```

## Subagent rules

Subagents inherit the parent's execution surface. Discovery warns about
and ignores these directories inside a subagent: `tools/`, `skills/`,
`extensions/`, `mcp-connections/`, `host-connections/`, `channels/`,
`schedules/`, `reminders/`, `hooks/`, `sandbox/`, and nested
`subagents/`.

The parent's [instructions](/docs/reference/instructions.md) should say when to
delegate, such as "When a request needs background research, delegate
to the `researcher` subagent."

## Subagents and peers

Subagents split one job into roles inside a single agent. When the
specialist is independently useful, with its own tools, sessions, and
playground, make it a full agent. See
[Peer agents](/docs/guides/agent-to-agent.md#peer-or-subagent).

---

Source: /docs/reference/tools.md

# Tools

A tool is a typed action the model can call, such as hitting an API, running a query, or writing a file. Each file in `bot/tools/` defines one tool, and the filename is the name the model sees. Server tools run on the serving host, and agent tools run as scripts next to the agent.

## Define a server tool

By default, `execute` runs in-process on the serving host with full
access to `process.env` and your `bot/lib/` code. `execution: "server"`
is the default.

A tool needs a filename slug (the model-facing name), a `description`
written for the model, an optional `inputSchema`, and the code that
runs it. With a Zod schema, Agent SDK validates the input and infers its type. With plain JSON Schema, `execute` gets raw JSON.

`prompt` from `@grok/agent-sdk` or `@grok/agent-sdk/prompt` dedents a
template literal so a multi-line description, reminder, or error can
sit indented in TypeScript. Blank lines and relative indentation stay.
`prompt.lines` returns the same text as `string[]`, one entry per line.

```ts
context: prompt.lines`
  Merged PR detected: ${pr.url} by ${author}.

  Call plan_deploy, then follow its nextStep.
`
```

```ts
import { prompt } from "@grok/agent-sdk";
import { defineTool } from "@grok/agent-sdk/tools";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineTool({
  description: prompt`
    Inspect a pull request before approval.
    Prefer this over guessing from the title alone.
  `,
  inputSchema: z.object({ prUrl: z.string().url() }),
  async execute({ prUrl }) {
    return { prUrl };
  },
});
```

### Tool context

`execute` receives a `ctx` with the runtime accessors:

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.toolCallId` | The call id, matching the `actions.requested` / `action.result` stream events |
| `ctx.session` | Read-only session info: id, channel, mode, auth |
| `ctx.approvedBy` | Auth of whoever approved a `needsApproval` call, same shape as `ctx.session.auth`. On Slack, `attributes.user_id` is the person who clicked Approve. Unset when the call needed no approval |
| `ctx.workspaceDir` | The session's workspace directory |
| `ctx.stateRoot` | The agent's durable state root, shared across every session |
| `ctx.host` | Shared host services (see below) |
| `ctx.send(channelId, message, options?)` | Start or resume a session on any channel. `auth` defaults to this call's session principal |
| `ctx.getSession(channelId, sessionId)` | Look up a session on a channel |
| `ctx.artifacts` | Session-bound [artifacts](/docs/reference/artifacts.md) facade: `tag` auto-fills the session |

`ctx.host` has `mcp`, `github`, `slack`, `kv`, `files`, and `reminders`.
Custom metrics use the [OpenTelemetry](/docs/guides/opentelemetry.md) API.

### Return values

`execute` may return a string, a JSON-shaped value, or `{ content: [...], isError? }`. Use object literals or `type` aliases, since an `interface` return fails typecheck with no index signature. If `execute` throws, the model gets the error and the turn keeps going.

### Declare structured output

Set `outputSchema` when MCP clients need a structured result contract. Use a
Zod schema or plain JSON Schema:

```ts
const Weather = z.object({
  city: z.string(),
  temperatureF: z.number(),
});

export default defineTool({
  description: "Read the current weather.",
  inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string() }),
  outputSchema: Weather,
  async execute({ city }) {
    return { city, temperatureF: 72 };
  },
});
```

Agent SDK advertises the schema and does not validate results against it.
A plain object fills MCP `structuredContent`. An envelope must set
`structuredContent` next to `content` and `isError`.

### Control dry-run effects

Set `effect` to `"read"`, `"write"`, `"idempotent"`, or a predicate over
the validated input. A dry-run session runs reads and stubs writes and
idempotent calls. A tool with no `effect` is a write. `"idempotent"` can
change something outside the session, and repeating the same arguments
has no further effect.

```ts
export default defineTool({
  description: "Publish a release.",
  inputSchema: z.object({ version: z.string() }),
  effect: "write",
  dryRunResult: ({ version }) => ({ published: false, version }),
  async execute({ version }) {
    return publishRelease(version);
  },
});
```

Set `dryRunResult` so a stubbed write returns the real shape. Without it, the write returns "Operation acknowledged." Traces mark the result as stubbed.

### Retry a transient read or idempotent call

If a read or an idempotent call fails with a transient error, Agent SDK
tries it up to 3 times before the model sees the error. It runs writes,
and tools that don't declare an effect, only once. Agent SDK retries an
MCP tool when the tool's annotations mark it read-only, or when the tool
sets `idempotentHint: true` together with an explicit `destructiveHint`.
If the call still fails, the tool error is the last attempt's message.

### Bound time arguments under `asOf`

`timeArgs` names the input fields that carry time bounds. In a session
created with `asOf`, each named argument must be an absolute ISO-8601
instant with a timezone, no later than that frozen instant. A missing,
relative, or later value is refused. Sessions without `asOf` ignore it.

```ts
export default defineTool({
  description: "Query telemetry between two instants.",
  inputSchema: z.object({ since: z.string(), until: z.string() }),
  effect: "read",
  timeArgs: ["since", "until"],
  async execute({ since, until }) {
    return queryTelemetry(since, until);
  },
});
```

Every name in `timeArgs` must exist in the input schema. A session with
`asOf` refuses to start otherwise, because a misspelled name would check
nothing.

## Define an agent tool

Set `execution: "agent"` when the tool must run next to the checkout.
The script receives JSON on stdin and prints its result on stdout.

```ts
export default defineTool({
  description: "Echo a message from the agent workspace.",
  execution: "agent",
  inputSchema: z.object({ message: z.string() }),
  script: `#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["message"])'
`,
});
```

Agent SDK copies the scripts into the workspace and lists them in the system prompt.

## Tools from an MCP connection, advertised by name

Set `advertiseTools: true` on a connection to expose its MCP tools by
name. Add per-session `auth` when credentials depend on the caller.
Model calls and [direct tool calls](#call-a-tool-without-a-model-turn)
use the same exposed names. See
[MCP connections](/docs/reference/connections.md#advertise-tools) for the full
contract.

## Call a tool without a model turn

You can call any server tool yourself, with your own input and no model turn. Validation and execution match a model-initiated call, and no Cursor API key is needed.

Over HTTP, with the same auth chain as the session API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/<slug>/v1/tools/inspect_pr \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":{"prUrl":"https://github.com/acme/checkout/pull/42"}}'
# {"ok":true,"toolName":"inspect_pr","callId":"tool_inspect_pr_…",
#  "isError":false,"result":{…},"durationMs":12}
```

From the CLI. Without `--url`, this starts an ephemeral server:

```text
agent-sdk tool call inspect_pr --dir . \
  --input '{"prUrl":"https://github.com/acme/checkout/pull/42"}'
```

Programmatically, `callTool(toolName, input, options?)` is available on
the serve handle, on channel route handlers and `onStart` args, and on
schedule `run` handlers, so a channel can mix deterministic calls with
model turns:

```ts
const outcome = await handle.callTool("inspect_pr", {
  prUrl: "https://github.com/acme/checkout/pull/42",
});
// { toolName, callId, isError, result, durationMs }
```

Omit both identifiers to run against an ephemeral workspace that is
removed when the call returns. Pass `sessionId` (HTTP body, `--session`,
or `options.sessionId`) or `continuationToken` (`<channelId>:<key>` as
`/v1/sessions` lists it) to bind the call. The two are mutually
exclusive.

| Rule | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Existing `sessionId`, or a token that maps to an existing session | Session workspace, owner check, and event recording |
| Token with no matching session | Scratch workspace; the token's channel id and key are the call identity |
| Busy session, `effect: "read"` (or an advertised MCP tool marked read-only) | Runs alongside the turn, reading the workspace as the turn left it; recorded under its own `turnId` |
| Busy session, write, idempotent, or undeclared | `409 session_busy` until the turn finishes |
| Session workspace cannot be created, read | Scratch workspace; the outcome has `scratchWorkspace: true` |
| Session workspace cannot be created, write | `500 workspace_unavailable` |

| Error | When |
| --- | --- |
| `404 unknown_tool` | Name is not a callable server tool; the response lists available names |
| `400 tool_not_callable` | Agent-execution tools cannot run on the host |
| `400 invalid_tool_input` | Zod rejected the input before `execute`. Plain JSON Schema is forwarded unvalidated |
| `400 invalid_continuation_token` | Malformed token, or passed together with `sessionId` |
| `404 session_not_found` | `sessionId` does not exist |
| `409 session_busy` | Write-effect call while a model turn is running |
| `500 workspace_unavailable` | Write-effect call when the session workspace cannot be created |
| `isError: true` | The tool body threw; same envelope the model would see |

See also [MCP connections](/docs/reference/connections.md), [Extensions](/docs/reference/extensions.md), and [Evals](/docs/evals.md).

---

Source: /docs/templates/agentic-owners.md

# Review pull requests with owners policies

This agent risk-tiers every pull request in your repository, requests
the owners as reviewers, and approves what your policy allows. Rules
live in `.agentic-owners/policy.yml` files at any depth. The closest policy to a changed file wins. The agent reads
policies from the PR's base ref, so a PR can't exempt itself.

## Scaffold and run

```bash
agent-sdk init ./owners-agent --template agentic-owners
```

Set your repositories in `bot/lib/config.ts` (`repos: ["acme/api"]`),
then run:

```bash
cd owners-agent
agent-sdk login
agent-sdk dev
```

PR events stream through your Cursor account, so you don't need a
webhook or GitHub App. The agent reviews a PR when it's opened,
reopened, pushed to, marked ready for review, or retargeted, and skips
drafts. Open a PR or replay a real one:

```bash
agent-sdk github replay https://github.com/acme/api/pull/123 --dir .
```

Deploy with `agent-sdk deploy`.

## Policies

With no policy files, the agent approves very-low and low risk PRs and
holds medium and above with a comment. Commit policies to route
reviews:

```yaml
# .agentic-owners/policy.yml at any depth; the closest policy wins.
version: 1
policies:
  - paths: ["docs/**"]
    always_approve: true
  - paths: ["src/api/**"]
    team: platform # bare slug in the repo's org; or acme/platform, or user: alice
    prompt: api-review.md # optional extra rubric, same directory
  - paths: ["src/billing/**"]
    users: [alice, bob]
    mode: hard # the agent never approves; a person must
```

`paths` are relative to the policy's parent directory, so
`src/.agentic-owners/policy.yml` matches `api/**` against `src/api/**`.
A leading `../` reaches a sibling tree inside the repo.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `paths` | Required globs |
| `team`, `teams` | Owner teams, as a slug in the repo's org or an `org/team` handle |
| `user`, `users` | Owner GitHub logins, without `@` |
| `prompt` | Extra rubric file beside the policy |
| `mode` | `advisory`, the default, approves low risk. `hard` requires a person to approve. `notify` never blocks and doesn't request its owners |
| `human_review_required` | `true` is the older spelling of `mode: hard` |
| `self_review` | A listed `user:` owner's own PRs clear this rule |
| `always_approve` | Satisfied at every risk tier. Allows no other key except `paths` |

- A rule without owners must set `always_approve: true`.
- `global_exclusions` in the root policy opts paths out entirely.
- The template rejects `delegated_automations`.

## What one review does

- One model turn per PR head grades the diff against the base rubric
  and matched rule prompts, then calls `record_review` with `very_low`,
  `low`, `medium`, `medium_high`, or `high`. The model never writes to
  GitHub.
- The host recomputes the policy from trusted state. It approves when
  every matched rule is `always_approve` or `notify`. Otherwise it
  approves only when the author's `self_review` clears every matched
  `hard` rule at very low or low risk, or every rule that can require
  review at medium and above.
- When the agent holds, it requests up to two owners, never the author,
  and updates one status comment in place.
- An approval binds to the head SHA. A later hold dismisses the agent's
  earlier approvals.
- The agent holds when the PR edits `.agentic-owners/` or `CODEOWNERS`,
  or when the diff is empty or GitHub truncated the diff or file list.
  `self_review` never clears a governance edit.
- A broken policy file fails closed and comments with the validation
  issues.

## Rubric

Edit `bot/lib/owners/prompts/base-review.md` to change the risk tiers.
Put per-area guidance in policy `prompt:` files.

## Evals

`agent-sdk eval` runs three smoke reviews without writing to GitHub.
They cover a docs-only change, an auth deletion, and a prompt injection.

---

Source: /docs/templates/reviews.md

# Review and triage templates

Each template is one model turn. A review template reads the diff and posts one comment, and the triage template comments on a ticket you already filed.

| Template | `--template` id | What it posts | Channel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Security reviewer | `security-reviewer` | One comment on exploitable bugs, such as injection, authz bypass, secret leaks, SSRF, and RCE | GitHub |
| Thermo review | `thermo-review` | One comment on bugs, breaking side effects, and unintended feature exposure | GitHub |
| Thermo quality review | `thermo-quality-review` | One comment on structure, such as missing abstractions, deep nesting, and files past 1,000 lines | GitHub |
| Triage | `triage-linear`, `triage-jira`, or `triage` | A `Triage:` comment, a bug priority, and a duplicate link when titles match | Linear or Jira |

`triage` is short for `triage-linear`. No review template comments on style, and the quality template doesn't argue about behavior.

The [Agentic Approver](/docs/templates/agentic-owners.md) template is separate. It applies an owners policy instead of posting one findings comment.

## Scaffold

```text
agent-sdk init ./security-reviewer --template security-reviewer \
  --var repos=acme/api
```

Swap the folder and the `--template` id for the row you want. `--var repos` is only for `security-reviewer`. Name repositories already connected in Cursor, separated by commas, and they must share one owner. `init` writes that list to `bot/lib/repos.ts`.

## Try it locally

Connect GitHub in Cursor for the repositories you watch (Settings or [cursor.com/dashboard](https://cursor.com/dashboard)), then sign the host in with `agent-sdk login`. The [GitHub guide](/docs/guides/github.md) covers `cursorAccount`.

```text
agent-sdk dev --cursor-events --repo acme/api
agent-sdk github replay https://github.com/acme/api/pull/12 --dir .
```

You need pull access to replay. The channel skips drafts, writes the diff to `pr/diff.patch`, and starts a turn. The model calls `post_findings` once, and that call writes the GitHub comment. Chat replies stay in the playground.

```text
agent-sdk eval
```

Eval sessions skip the GitHub write. Edit `bot/instructions.md` for what counts as a finding, and edit `evals/review.eval.ts` for the smoke cases.

## Deploy

From the agent's git checkout:

```text
agent-sdk login
agent-sdk deploy --cursor-events-repo acme/api
```

Repeat `--cursor-events-repo` for each repository, and every repository must share one owner. The deployment watches those repositories through your team's Cursor GitHub connection, and you can change the list later without a redeploy:

```text
agent-sdk deployment update my-agent --event-repo acme/api --event-repo acme/web
```

## Triage a tracker

The template runs after someone files a ticket, so keep filing them as you do now. Connect Linear or Jira under MCP in the Cursor dashboard, then run `agent-sdk dev` and open `/queue/issue` in the playground.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/triage-agent/v1/channels/queue/issue \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "identifier": "ENG-142",
    "title": "CSV export returns 500",
    "description": "Export has returned 500 since this morning."
  }'
```

For create webhooks, set `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` or `JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and point the provider at `/v1/channels/webhook` on the deployed alias. `record_triage` comments on the issue that started the session. Edit `bot/skills/triage-rubric.md` for kinds and what `urgent` means on your team. Eval sessions skip tracker writes.

---

Source: /docs/troubleshooting.md

# Fix common agent problems

Start with three checks:

1. Run `agent-sdk validate --dir .`.
2. Confirm the expected agent and connections in
   `agent-sdk info --dir . --json`.
3. Reproduce the problem once, then read the serve log or the
   [session trace](#read-the-session-trace).

## Serve or the playground won't work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The playground is blank or lists no agents | Start `agent-sdk serve`, because the playground gets its agents from the server. |
| Agent-file edits don't appear | Open the URL that `serve --dev` prints, and press Enter in its terminal to reload. |
| Sessions exist but the list is empty | The list shows only your own sessions, so use the identity that created them. |

## A turn fails or misbehaves

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Reads and greps keep failing with `NGHTTP2_FRAME_SIZE_ERROR` | Run the agent under Node 22.13 or newer, never Bun. |
| `Semantic search has been removed. Use Grep.` | Delete `search` from a custom `fs`, drop `SearchQuery` and `SearchResult`, and remove `SemanticSearch` or `semSearch` from `tools` and `bot/tools/`. |
| The turn reports a missing API key | Set `CURSOR_API_KEY`, `CURSOR_API_KEY_FILE`, or `CURSOR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY`, or run `agent-sdk login`. |
| Login works but the model host rejects the key | Point `CURSOR_API_BASE_URL` and `CURSOR_BACKEND_URL` at the same API host. |
| The first turn reports `[resource_exhausted]` | The model is usually out of capacity. If a GitHub event started the turn, check for a GitHub `429` rate-limit response first. |
| Replies quote an ancestor `AGENTS.md` or unrelated repository rules | Set `defineAgent({ local: { cwd } })` so the agent doesn't inherit the parent checkout. `/v1/info` shows the current `local.cwd`. |
| The model lists IDE meta-tools but never calls named MCP tools | Set `advertiseTools: true` on the local connection. |
| Server tools, skills, or seed files are missing | Check the discovered project in `/v1/info`, and follow the warning from `validate`. |
| `validate` and `run` pass but CI type-checking fails | Return JSON-shaped tool results, such as object literals or `type` aliases, instead of `interface` types. |

## HTTP returns 401, 403, or 409

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `401` outside local development | Send the bearer token, alias token, or channel credential. Default custom routes accept only direct loopback calls. |
| `403` on a stream or follow-up | Use the identity that created the session. |
| A custom route fails through a tunnel or LAN | Protect the host with `--bearer-token` or channel auth. Use `--allow-anonymous` only behind a proxy that authenticates every caller. |
| `409` on a follow-up | Refresh the rotating `continuationToken`. Task sessions don't accept follow-ups. |
| `409 session_busy` from `call --session` | Wait for the turn, omit `--session`, or mark a read-only tool `effect: "read"` so it can run alongside the turn. |

## A hosted deployment fails or looks stale

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `validate` or `deploy` reports `architecture "v2" requires a named secret` | Replace the literal or getter with a [named secret](/docs/deployment.md#add-egress-and-secrets), and set its value with `agent-sdk secret set <slug> NAME`. |
| Local changes don't appear after deploy | `deploy` builds the pushed ref, so commit and push your changes, then deploy again. |
| The deployment never reaches `running` | Run `agent-sdk deployment get <slug>`, and fix the error it reports. |
| A secret or egress change has no effect | Confirm the name with `secret list`, check that the `hosting` block is on the pushed ref, and redeploy. |
| A hosted schedule doesn't fire | Check that the deployment is running and that the schedule is in `bot/schedules/` on the deployed ref. |
| A custom route returns `429` | Wait for the time in `Retry-After`, then send it again. |

## GitHub deliveries fail

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `github forward` gets `401` on every delivery | Clear the token variables so the forwarder uses your `gh` login, as in `GITHUB_TOKEN= GH_TOKEN= agent-sdk github forward`. |
| `Hook already exists` | Stop the stale forwarder. GitHub allows one per repository. |
| Direct webhooks are rejected outside `--dev` | Set the same `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` on the signer and the server. |
| You can't create a forwarder | Use `agent-sdk github replay <pr-url>`, which needs only pull access. |

## Slack doesn't respond

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Logs say `channel idle ... missing credentials` | Run `agent-sdk slack create --dir <agent>`, then check the prefix with `agent-sdk slack doctor`. |
| `slack create` waits for workspace approval | Keep the CLI running and open the **Request approval** link it prints. After an admin approves, select **Retry** in the [Deployed Agents](https://cursor.com/dashboard/deployed-agents) **Add Slack** wizard. |
| The bot ignores ordinary channel posts | Configure `engagement.channelPosts`, create the app with `--channel-posts`, and invite it to each allowed channel. |

## MCP authorization fails

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `must be defineConnection({ url, oauth: true })` | Add `oauth: true` to the connection, or fix the filename you passed to `mcp oauth`. |
| Local auth works but hosted calls return unauthorized | Your local OAuth tokens don't reach a deployment. Use a `cursorAccount: true` connection, as described in [Host MCP OAuth](/docs/guides/mcp-oauth.md#use-an-oauth-server-from-a-hosted-agent). |
| The model invents `mcp_auth` instead of calling the server | Set `advertiseTools: true` for named local tools, or expose a wrapper through `ctx.host.mcp`. |

## Schedules or reminders stall

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| A schedule or reminder never fires under `--dev` | `--dev` doesn't fire them on its own, so trigger one through its `/v1/dev/schedules/<id>` or `/v1/dev/reminders/<id>` route. |
| A reminder is disarmed with `handler_lost_on_restart` | Recreate handler-form reminders after a restart, or use a prompt-form reminder. |
| One schedule fires on several self-hosted processes | Pass `--no-schedules` to every serving process but one. |

## Read the session trace

```bash
agent-sdk session list --prod --slug <slug>
agent-sdk session get <sessionId> --prod --slug <slug> --view events
agent-sdk session get --file <trace-path>
```

Find a hosted session with `session list`, then print its events with
`--view events`. For a local run, pass the trace path from `agent-sdk run`
to `--file`. Pair each `actions.requested` event with its `action.result`
to find the call that failed.
